definitions.explanation: Not meeting the required standard of quality or function. Used for products, conditions, health, and performance.
A young person who engages in antisocial or rebellious behavior. A cultural archetype in Japanese media, especially associated with the stereotypical rebel image of the 1980s and 1990s.

examples.japanese: {不良|ふりょう}{品|ひん}を{交換|こうかん}してもらった。
examples.english: I had the defective product exchanged.

examples.japanese: {姿勢|しせい}が{不良|ふりょう}だと{腰痛|ようつう}の{原因|げんいん}になる。
examples.english: Bad posture can cause lower back pain.

examples.japanese: {寝不足|ねぶそく}で{体調|たいちょう}{不良|ふりょう}になった。
examples.english: I became unwell due to lack of sleep.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}の{前|まえ}に{不良|ふりょう}がたむろしていた。
examples.english: Delinquents were hanging around in front of the school.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}は{不良|ふりょう}だったらしい。
examples.english: Apparently, he was a delinquent when he was young.

examples.japanese: {不良|ふりょう}マンガのブームは1980{年代|ねんだい}にピークを{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: The boom in delinquent manga peaked in the 1980s.

notes:
{不良|ふりょう} has two major uses.

Sense 1 (defective/bad) is common in formal and technical contexts:
- {不良|ふりょう}{品|ひん} (defective product)
- {体調|たいちょう}{不良|ふりょう} (poor health condition)
- {接触|せっしょく}{不良|ふりょう} (poor contact/loose connection)
- {不良|ふりょう}{債権|さいけん} (bad debt, non-performing loan)

Sense 2 (delinquent) refers to a cultural archetype:
- {不良|ふりょう}{少年|しょうねん}/{少女|しょうじょ} (delinquent boy/girl)
- The stereotypical image includes a modified school uniform, pompadour hairstyle, and motorcycle
- This image is heavily featured in manga and anime genres like {ヤンキー} culture
